title: OpenPLC Editor
subtitle: desktop IEC 61131-3 PLC programming IDE (Electron + React)
advisorySource: GitHub Advisory Database via osv-scanner (OSV) (equivalent to Dependabot)
_note_ids: Every triage entry lists the advisory ids it accounts for. build-report.mjs cross-checks the live post-suppression scan against these: an advisory no entry claims is reported in section 4a as untriaged instead of being silently omitted.
_note_counts: advisories/counts describe the last FULL assessment and are only rendered when the report is built without a live scan. With --osv-raw/--osv-delta the numbers come from that run.
headline: No reachability assessment has been recorded yet for this product. The advisory numbers in this report come from the live scan; every advisory surfacing after the VEX baseline is listed in section 4a until it is triaged.
scope: OpenPLC Editor is a desktop IDE for programming PLCs in the IEC 61131-3 languages, built with Electron and React and distributed as installers built by electron-builder. This assessment covers the complete transitive npm dependency graph resolved in package-lock.json (build and renderer) and release/app/package-lock.json (native runtime modules packaged with the app).
scopeNote: The SBOM covers the npm dependency graph. Not in it: the Electron/Chromium runtime binaries downloaded by electron-builder, artifacts fetched at install or build time from pinned manifests (the WebAssembly Python runtime and its wheels in python-runtime.json, the STruCpp compiler release in binary-versions.json), the toolchain packages whose licences live in third-party-licenses/, and the C/C++ sources vendored under resources/sources/.
methodologyNote: Advisory data was obtained from the GitHub Advisory Database via osv-scanner (OSV) (equivalent to GitHub Dependabot alerts). The source of truth for shipped versions is the committed lockfiles (package-lock.json and release/app/package-lock.json).
remediation: Triage every advisory listed in section 4a and record a CISA VEX determination for each in security/report-config.json or osv-scanner.toml.

practices.practice: Deterministic installs from a committed lockfile (npm ci in CI)
SBOM generated per release in CycloneDX and SPDX
CI security gate runs on every pull request and blocks newly-introduced critical advisories
That gate configured as a required status check, so it blocks the merge
